Amandeep: Saurabh, I saw you at the bus stop at 9 today. Aren't you supposed to be at work?
Saurabh: ...
Amandeep: You can tell me
Saurabh: I was laid off three weeks ago
Amandeep: Three weeks? Do your parents know?
Saurabh: No. I leave home every morning and sit in the library. I couldn't face it
Amandeep: That must be exhausting
Saurabh: It is. And I missed a job lead. my uncle's friend was hiring, but I couldn't ask
Amandeep: Because that means telling them
Saurabh: yes
Amandeep: Tell them tonight. I'll sit outside if it helps
Saurabh: ok. ok

qa.q: How long ago was Saurabh laid off?
qa.a: Saurabh was laid off three weeks ago.

qa.q: What was Saurabh feeling when hiding the layoff?
qa.a: Saurabh felt ashamed and worn out, and could not face telling the family, so kept leaving home each morning.

qa.q: What could Saurabh do tonight, and why?
qa.a: Saurabh could tell the family about the layoff and ask for leads, because the secret adds stress and hides possible help.

qa.q: How might Saurabh's parents feel on learning about the three weeks?
qa.a: They may feel worried and hurt at being kept out, but also relieved to be able to help and share leads.

grounding: Ashamed of a layoff, a person leaves home each morning and tells no one, which adds stress and cuts off leads and support.

subtype: Approach: hide the news from family to avoid worry [Pitfall]
passage:
Every morning at 7:30, Tejas still packed his tiffin, touched his grandmother's feet and caught the bus from Karad toward the industrial estate. The spinning mill had let him go three weeks earlier. He hadn't told anyone.
He spent the days at the bus stand, then the temple steps, then a tea stall where no one knew him, refreshing job sites on his phone. He came home at six, said 'Tiring day,' and ate quietly.
He wasn't sleeping. He had started snapping at his younger sister over nothing.
One Sunday, at a cousin's naming ceremony, his uncle Chetan mentioned loudly that the sugar factory in Satara had been hiring machine operators. 'Interviews finished last week, though. Would've suited someone like Tejas, if he wasn't settled already.'
Tejas smiled, nodded and felt his stomach drop. He had missed a job his own family could have pointed him to, because he'd been too ashamed to say one sentence at home.

qa.q: Where did Tejas spend his days after the layoff?
qa.a: At the bus stand, then the temple steps, then a tea stall where no one knew him.

qa.q: What was Tejas feeling when his uncle mentioned the sugar factory?
qa.a: His stomach dropped; he felt sick with regret and shame at missing a lead his family could have given him.

qa.q: What small step could Tejas take now?
qa.a: Tell one person at home, perhaps Chetan, what happened, so the family can share leads and support instead of him carrying it alone.

qa.q: What is it like for Tejas's younger sister these weeks?
qa.a: She is snapped at for nothing and doesn't know why, so the secret is hurting her too.

grounding: Shows a laid-off young man leaving home each morning and telling no one, which adds stress and cuts him off from a family lead.

subtype: Approach: hide the news from family to avoid worry [Pitfall]
passage:
Emil had lost his warehouse-software job in Hamburg on a Tuesday, and by Friday he had a routine: shower, shirt, bag, out of the flat by eight, so his mother and his stepfather, Tariq, would think he was going to work. He spent the days in the public library and a cheap café, applying for jobs and checking his bank balance.
He told himself he was protecting them. Tariq had his own worries at the port.
But the secret grew heavy. He jumped when his phone rang. He lied about lunch, about a colleague's birthday, about why he was home at three one Thursday.
Six weeks in, at dinner, Tariq mentioned that a logistics firm he worked with was desperate for someone who understood warehouse systems. 'I told them I didn't know anyone.' Emil stared at his plate. Three minutes later, he told them everything. His mother's first words were, 'Why did you carry this alone?'

qa.q: What time did Emil leave the flat each morning?
Why did Emil keep the layoff secret?
qa.a: He felt ashamed, and told himself he was protecting his mother and Tariq from worry.

qa.q: What could Emil have done in the first week instead?
qa.a: Told his mother and Tariq early, so their support and leads, like the logistics job, could reach him sooner.

qa.q: What might Emil's mother feel when she hears the truth?
qa.a: Hurt that he carried it alone for six weeks, but mostly concerned and relieved to finally be able to help.

grounding: Shows a laid-off young man pretending to go to work and hiding it from family, adding stress and nearly missing a lead they could offer.
